jobs.title: President & CEO
jobs.description:
ORGANIZATION:
East Bay Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (East Bay SPCA), founded in 1874, is proud to be one of the oldest shelters in the country and one of the most innovative in their region. Their mission is to transform the lives of cats and dogs by enriching the human-animal bond through respected and accessible expertise. They are a local non-profit that is not affiliated with any national organization. The organization is comprised of a strategic and engaged Board of Directors, experienced executive leadership, and a talented, energetic, dedicated and committed staff.

The organization is supported by approximately 100 staff and 500+ active volunteers. They have an annual operating budget of approximately $14 million and an endowment of $30 million. Their main campus is located in Oakland, with an adoption center in Dublin and spay/neuter surgery center also in Oakland.

In 2025, East Bay SPCA facilitated more than 2,700 adoptions, distributed pet food to nearly 700 households, and benefited from more than 35,000 volunteer hours.

REPORTING RELATIONSHIP:
The President & CEO reports directly to the Board of Directors.

POSITION SUMMARY:
East Bay SPCA is seeking a President & Chief Executive Officer who is excited to inherit a skilled and dedicated organization recognized in the community as a leader in animal welfare. The President & CEO will bring proven experience building strategic plans, an experienced fundraiser and leading strong operational and financial performance, and will foster a culture of trust, collaboration, and accountability.

The ideal candidate will be a highly collaborative thinker with experience in managing nonprofit organizations. Previous animal welfare experience is not required but preferred. Prior extensive experience with nonprofit fundraising is required. This role will focus 60% of their time externally (fundraising,government/external affairs, visible thought leader and brand advocate) and 40% internally (operations, finance, human resources and shelter & veterinary administration).

Key staff that report to the CEO include the Vice President of Finance, Vice President of Medical Services, Vice President of Operations and Vice President of Philanthropy.

SCOPE AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
The President & CEO will be responsible for the following areas:
I. LEADERSHIP OF THE ORGANIZATION

Staff

Serve as an advocate for staff. Ensure the recognition of excellence in employee performance, as well as the development of employees’ skills and effectiveness at the organization.
Build and sustain a high-performing, mission-driven leadership team.
Develop, retain, and attract exceptional talent at all levels of the organization, that delivers specific measurable results in all aspects of EBSPCA’s deliverables.
Foster an organizational culture characterized by trust, collaboration, accountability, inclusion, transparency, and respect.
Ensure employees have the resources, support, development opportunities, and leadership necessary to perform at their best.
Recognize the emotional demands inherent in animal welfare and veterinary work and promote a healthy, sustainable workplace.
Champion professional development, succession planning, leadership development, and organizational learning.
Lead the strategic planning and implementation of EBSPCA’s strategic plan.

Board

Develop a strong, transparent, and trusting partnership with the Board Chair and Board of Directors.
Provide the Board with timely, accurate, and meaningful information necessary for effective governance and decision-making. Ensure periodic and proactive reporting to the Board on the financial and operational status of EBSPCA that includes key metrics.
Support the Board in strategic planning, policy development, financial oversight, CEO evaluation, and organizational stewardship.
Engage Board members according to their individual expertise, networks, resources, and capacity to advance the mission.
Ensure the Board is aligned with the organization's vision and goals.

II. DEVELOPMENT/MARKETING/COMMUNICATIONS

Working with the Vice President of Philanthropy, expand and enhance a diversified fundraising program that includes, but is not limited to, major individual giving, planned giving, foundation, corporate, government, in-kind, and special events.
Serve as the organization’s chief ambassador and principal relationship builder with major donors, foundations, corporations, community leaders, and other stakeholders.
Partner closely with the philanthropy team and Board to strengthen a culture of philanthropy throughout the organization.
Personally cultivate, solicit, and steward significant individual and institutional donors.
Build and deepen relationships with high-capacity Bay Area philanthropists and animal welfare supporters.
Engage Board members and other volunteer leaders as effective ambassadors and fundraisers.
Establish community and business partnerships to achieve EBSPCA’s vision.
Act as the lead spokesperson for EBSPCA and represent EBSPCA at public functions.
Cultivate and develop increased visibility of EBSPCA and foster excellent public relations to enhance the organization’s image and the stature of those served by EBSPCA.
Ensure that fundraising strategy is closely connected to compelling organizational priorities, outcomes, and stories of impact.
Working with the Vice President of Philanthropy, responsible for developing and implementing the marketing and communications plan.
Strengthen the organization’s visibility and influence throughout the East Bay and greater Bay Area.
Build strong relationships with government officials, municipal animal services, veterinarians, animal welfare organizations, foundations, corporations, community organizations, media, and other strategic partners.
Develop collaborative partnerships that expand access to veterinary care, behavioral resources, pet support, education, adoption, and other services.
Take an active role as a thought leader in animal welfare.

III. FINANCE/OPERATIONS/ADMINISTRATION

Maintain rigorous financial oversight and ensure the long-term financial health and sustainability of the organization.
Develop and manage an annual budget and operating plan for the organization, as well as maintain an appropriate cash reserve.
Work closely with the Vice President of Finance, Board Finance and Audit Committees on budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, investment decisions, and risk management.
Working with the Vice President of Operations and Vice President of Finance on the organization’s operational and capital fiscal performance.
Align financial resources with strategic priorities and organizational impact.
Develop diversified and sustainable revenue strategies.
Ensure responsible stewardship of donor and community resources.
Execute the strategic plan, driving towards desired outcomes. Report on said outcomes. Ensure that quality data is captured, analyzed, and utilized to inform data-driven decisions. Based on operating results and data analysis, make the appropriate adjustments and/or recommendations to influence the plan/strategy going forward.
Provide effective leadership of the organization’s programs, operations, medical services, finance, philanthropy, human resources, communications, and other functions.
Establish clear expectations, accountability, decision-making processes, and performance measures for the senior leadership team.
Ensure that animal care, veterinary medicine, sheltering, adoption, behavior and training, foster care, education, and community programs operate at the highest standards.
Maintain a strong culture of safety, compassion, professionalism, accountability, inclusion, and continuous improvement.
Ensure appropriate organizational infrastructure, policies, technology, systems, and talent are in place to support future growth.
Effectively manage organizational risk, regulatory compliance, insurance, legal matters, and reputational considerations.

IV. PROGRAMS AND ANIMAL WELFARE

Working with the Vice Presidents of Medical Services and Operations, ensure the highest standards of animal welfare, veterinary medicine, shelter operations, adoption, foster care, behavior, training, and enrichment.
Promote evidence-based approaches to animal welfare and positive-reinforcement training.
Ensure that organizational decisions reflect both compassion and sound professional judgment.
Support continued innovation in preventing animal homelessness and addressing the underlying challenges facing pets and their families.
Maintain a strong commitment to accessibility and to removing barriers that prevent community members from obtaining animal welfare resources.
Ensure that the organization remains focused on measurable outcomes for both animals and people.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Twelve+ years in an executive leadership role for a nonprofit.
At least five years of experience as a CEO, President, Executive Director or comparable senior executive with broad leadership experience.
Experience leading a complex nonprofit organization with significant operating scale, multiple programs and/or locations, substantial staff, and a similar sized annual budget.
Demonstrated fundraising success, including major gifts and relationships with high-capacity donors, foundations, corporations, and other philanthropic partners.
Experience in building, motivating, and developing staff as an effective leader within a cross-functional team setting.

EDUCATION:
A bachelor’s degree is required. An advanced degree would be preferred.

jobs.description:
About San Francisco Compute

San Francisco Compute exists to give ambitious teams large scale supercomputers without taking on a catastrophic balance sheet risk. Most GPU clouds force you to sign long term contracts with no way out. If you underbuy, you miss the window. If you overbuy, you’ll blow up with no way out. It’s a desperate gamble that San Francisco Compute does not force you to play.

Originally, SFC was an AI lab that bought too big of a GPU cluster and was forced to sublease it or go under. Today, we build data centers, supercomputers, and then lease those machines on contracts that let our customers sublease. More than anyone else in the industry, we deeply felt the pain and fear of being forced to bet the farm with your neocloud vendor. To make it possible to sublease, we invented the first compute market and became the first one to offer physical settlement. That means we operate GPU clusters like a neocloud and derisk our customers like a market.

Customers buying GPU clusters don’t want to work through a network of brokers. They want to transact with the folks that have the keys to the cluster and can own the SLA.

To keep the industry safe from unnecessary risk, SFC needs to scale fast. To do that, we serve financially motivated parties as a technical partner to build, operate, & lease supercomputers on their behalf. Basically, we help folks who want an economic return build GPU clusters on their balance sheet, but operated in full by us. That allows us to retain the technical control needed to operate a cloud, but scale fast like a market. SFC’s ability to offer subleasing can significantly increase the levered returns for cluster owners. Our hybrid model out-performs brokered contracts or other “compute markets”, who have to go through a network of counterparties to solve problems. It also lets us design custom solutions for our customers, like clusters deployed in regions next to your dataset or physical eval set or a large CPU fleet deployed colocated with your GPU cluster.

Our team includes senior & technical leadership from places like Lambda, Crusoe, Digital Ocean, AWS, and Hut8. Our CTO is the cofounder and former CEO of Voltage Park. In prior roles, our team has deployed 8GW of datacenter capacity & hundreds of thousands of GPUs. We’ve been described as having “the highest talent density in the space.” If you are an honorable, gritty person with eyes wide open & good epistemics, who wants to see AI go right, we’d love to work with you. There has never been a more critical moment in history and it is up to us to shape it on behalf of those who come after us.

About The Role

SF Compute is seeking a Chief of Staff to the CEO to serve as a partner and force multiplier to the CEO. This role combines operations, and execution, working closely with the CEO on the highest-impact priorities and decisions shaping the company’s future. The Chief of Staff will drive cross-functional initiatives, help translate company priorities into action across the leadership team, and ensure key decisions move from alignment to measurable outcomes across the organization. This role is a hybrid role and requires 3-5 days in-person presence in our San Francisco office.

What You Will Do

Serve as a trusted partner to the CEO to execute the goals & vision of the company.
Help identify organizational bottlenecks and ambiguous problems, structure them into actionable plans, and drive resolution with the right owners.
Translate and coordinate key decisions, analysis, and recommendations into clear actions the leadership team can execute quickly by aligning stakeholders and following through on commitments.
Build enough understanding of our business, market, financing, and deal dynamics to engage in strategic discussions and tradeoffs.
Represent the CEO in select internal and external conversations with customers, partners, and stakeholders.

Who You Are

Strong technical fluency and ability to engage with Engineering, GTM, and Product leaders on complex topics (AI/ML, infrastructure, architecture, etc.)
Experience operating in high-growth, P0-to-1 environments where priorities evolve quickly.
High-agency operator who takes ownership, works through ambiguity, and closes loops without needing direction.
Trusted, discreet, and low ego, with strong judgment around sensitive information and relationships.
Strong communicator who can create alignment internally and represent the company externally when needed.

Benefits

Visa Sponsorships

Medical, dental & vision

Time off

We offer unlimited paid time off as well as 10+ observed holidays

Parental leave

We offer biological, adoptive, and foster parents paid time off to spend quality time with family

jobs.description:
Background

JOB DESCRIPTION

UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security.

The Division of Finance and Administration (DFA) is responsible for the planning, allocation and management of financial and administrative resources including information communications and technology, procurement and travel, security and safety, facility and general operational management. The DFA is responsible for the effective and efficient delivery of essential operations services in UN Women, continuous development and improvement in operations, policies, procedures and guidance to align with UN Women and stakeholders' evolving business needs, and technical and advisory support to the Executive Director in the formulation and implementation of the UN Women overall mission.

Reporting to the Chief Finance Officer and Director, DFA, the Deputy Director for Financial Management leads the Financial Management Section and UN Women’s global finance function. The role oversees financial operations, accounting and treasury services, financial policies and controls, ERP-enabled financial processes, IPSAS-compliant financial statements, donor and management reporting, audit engagement, and financial risk management across a decentralized operating environment.

Key Functions And Accountabilities

The Deputy Director for Financial Management leads UN Women’s global financial management function and is responsible for ensuring effective stewardship of financial resources, sound financial operations, strong internal controls, timely IPSAS-compliant reporting, effective treasury and revenue management, and continuous improvement of finance policies, systems and processes.

Strategic financial leadership and accountability

Lead the Financial Management Section and global finance network, setting priorities, workplans, performance standards and accountability mechanisms aligned with UN Women’s Strategic Plan and business needs.
Provide strategic advice to the CFO and Director, DFA, senior management and governance bodies on financial management, financial risk, resource stewardship and organizational sustainability.
Promote clear accountability, transparency and consistency across financial operations, reporting, field support and financial advisory services.
Lead engagement with senior stakeholders to ensure finance priorities support organizational strategy, operational effectiveness and accountability for results.

Financial policy, controls and risk management

Maintain and continuously strengthen UN Women’s financial framework, including financial regulations and rules, policies, procedures, delegations of authority, guidance and internal controls.
Ensure effective first- and second-line controls over financial management processes, monitor exceptions and support risk management, business continuity and compliance activities.
Oversee financial due diligence and provide advice on donor agreements, cost recovery, revenue recognition and financial clauses in legal instruments.
Approve, monitor and report on policy exceptions, including emergency or special operating procedures, ensuring appropriate controls and documentation.

Financial operations, revenue and treasury management

Oversee headquarters and field financial operations, including transaction recording, general ledger integrity, vendor and payment controls, partner advance monitoring, project closure and management reporting.
Lead centralized revenue management, including recording of contributions, accounts receivable, non-core cash allocations, donor agreement finance data and related reconciliations.
Ensure effective management of cash, bank positions, investments, foreign exchange and treasury-related risks in coordination with relevant UN system service providers and governance mechanisms.
Ensure financial transactions and balances are accurately processed, recorded, reconciled and monitored to support reliable financial information and timely decision-making.

Financial reporting, IPSAS compliance and donor reporting

Lead month-end, mid-year and year-end closure processes, including issuance of instructions, account reconciliations, review of financial data and timely resolution of material issues.
Lead the preparation, review and certification of UN Women’s IPSAS-compliant annual financial statements, audit working papers and financial inputs to Executive Board and senior management reporting.
Ensure timely and accurate donor financial reporting, certified donor statements, pooled or inter-agency funding reports, specialized financial reports and internal management reports.
Provide financial analysis and reporting to support senior management decisions, Executive Board engagement, donor stewardship and organizational performance monitoring.

Audit, oversight and assurance

Manage financial management engagement with the United Nations Board of Auditors, internal audit, donor assurance reviews, third-party partner audits, EU verifications, JIU reviews and other oversight bodies.
Coordinate timely responses to audit inquiries, findings and recommendations; oversee corrective actions; and report on implementation and emerging financial risks.
Provide financial assurance advice and support to headquarters, regional and country offices before, during and after audits and reviews.
Identify recurring assurance issues and drive systemic improvements to strengthen financial governance, compliance and risk mitigation across the organization.

Business transformation, ERP and process improvement

Lead continuous improvement of financial management processes, with emphasis on simplification, harmonization, automation, management by exception, ERP optimization and technology-enabled solutions.
Support UN reform and efficiency initiatives, participate in inter-agency finance and accounting standard-setting groups, and contribute to resource mobilization and innovative financing initiatives.
Ensure financial systems and related tools are configured and functioning to manage, monitor and report on key financial processes and information.
Champion data-quality, analytics and digital finance capabilities that improve insight, efficiency and accountability across global financial management.

Representation, knowledge management and capacity building

Represent UN Women and the Financial Management Section in internal governance bodies, Executive Board-related processes, UN inter-agency fora and oversight, advisory, investment and compliance committees.
Provide financial management guidance to headquarters and field offices and strengthen the global finance community through learning, technical guidance, communities of practice and on-the-job capacity building.
Lead, motivate and develop finance staff, promoting collaboration, accountability, service orientation and high standards of professional performance.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities:
The incumbent leads a diverse and expert team, which includes professional and general service staff, as well as affiliate personnel (PSA, consultants and interns).

Integrity;
Professionalism;
Respect for Diversity.

Accountability;
Creative Problem Solving;
Effective Communication;

Please visit this link for more information on UN Women’s Values and Competencies Framework:

Functional Competencies

Demonstrated success in leading and implementing financial re-engineering, management systems development, policy design, innovation, knowledge product development in large and or multinational organizations/corporation.

Recruitment Qualifications

Experience

Experience with ERP-enabled financial management systems, preferably Oracle Cloud or another UN system ERP, is required.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Scion Executive Search has been retained to conduct an immediate search for the Executive Director
of Animal Humane New Mexico
, an organization that supports and improves the lives of New Mexico’s cats and dogs through sheltering, adoptions, humane education, and veterinary services.
This is a full-time, onsite position based in Albuquerque, NM.

ABOUT ANIMAL HUMANE NEW MEXICO:

Animal Humane New Mexico (AHNM) is a shelter located in the heart of New Mexico, driven by the belief that every adoptable animal deserves the love of a home, and every home deserves the transformative love of a pet. Through community outreach and shelter animal transfer efforts, Animal Humane helps improve the lives of cats and dogs across the state, providing support to more than 10,000 homeless and at-risk animals each year

AHNM's impact reaches well beyond the shelter walls through a comprehensive network of programs serving animals and pet owners alike. Its Behavior Support team provides enrichment and training to hundreds of shelter and owned pets each year, addressing the root causes that separate pets from their families. Its Pet Resource Center, the first of its kind in New Mexico, keeps owned pets happy, healthy, and with the families who love them. Its donor-subsidized Veterinary Clinic delivers reduced-cost care to shelter animals and low-income pet owners, ensuring veterinary access is never a barrier to keeping a family together. The Animal Humane Thrift Shop rounds out this network, turning everyday donations into direct funding for the thousands of animals who pass through the shelter's doors each year.

Rooted in community and driven by compassion, Animal Humane has grown into a trusted, multifaceted resource for animals and pet owners across New Mexico, one that meets need wherever it exists, from the shelter floor to the exam room to the front porch of a family working to keep their pet at home.

This is a remarkable moment to join an organization whose work not only saves and improves the lives of thousands of animals each year, but also strengthens the bond between pets and the families who love them. AHNM’s next leader will help shape the organization's future at a time when compassionate, community-driven animal welfare leadership is more essential than ever.

POSITION OVERVIEW:

The Executive Director is responsible for the overall leadership, strategic direction, and operational management of the organization in accordance with the mission, policies, and strategic direction established by the Board of Directors. This role provides visionary leadership to advance the organization’s lifesaving mission while ensuring operational excellence across all departments, including Marketing and Development, Veterinary Clinic, Volunteer Services, Community Programs, Pet Pathways, Lifesaving Programs, Thrift Shop Operations, Facilities, Human Resources, Finance, and Executive Administration.

Serving as the primary liaison between the Board of Directors and staff, the Executive Director implements board policies, manages organizational resources, leads the senior leadership team, and ensures the effective delivery of programs and services. The Executive Director also serves as a key ambassador for the organization, strengthening community relationships, fundraising efforts, and partnerships within the animal welfare field.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Organizational Leadership & Strategy

Provide visionary leadership and strategic direction aligned with the mission and goals of Animal Humane New Mexico, developing priorities in partnership with the Board of Directors.
Ensure alignment between strategy, programs, and operations, and lead the senior leadership team to strong organizational performance.
Monitor performance and community impact, fostering a culture of collaboration, accountability, and mission-driven work.

Board Relations & Governance

Serve as primary staff liaison to the Board, providing timely information to support decision-making.
Partner with the Board President on meeting agendas and strategic discussions, and support board engagement in planning, fundraising, and advocacy.
Ensure compliance with bylaws, governance standards, and nonprofit best practices.

Departmental Oversight

Provide leadership and strategic oversight across: Marketing & Development, Volunteer Services, Veterinary Clinic (ensuring compliance with the Veterinary Practice Act and high medical standards), Community Programs, Pet Pathways, Lifesaving Programs, Thrift Shop Operations, Facilities, Human Resources, Finance, and Executive Administration (including supervision of the Executive Assistant).

Financial Oversight

Ensure responsible financial management and long-term fiscal sustainability, overseeing the annual budget with the Finance Director and Board.
Provide regular financial reporting, maintain strong controls and risk management, and ensure transparency in the use of resources.
Lead fundraising strategy, cultivating relationships with major donors, foundations, and corporate partners; partner with Development and Marketing on donor engagement and actively participate in cultivation and outreach efforts.

Program Oversight

Ensure programs effectively support the mission and strategic goals, monitoring outcomes and operational performance.
Support innovation and continuous improvement, ensuring alignment with community needs and industry best practices.
Staff Leadership & Culture
Recruit, develop, and retain a strong leadership team, providing supervision and coaching.
Foster a culture of compassion, respect, and accountability, ensuring staff and volunteers have the resources and training to succeed.

Community & External Relations

Serve as primary spokesperson and ambassador for the organization, building relationships with donors, community organizations, government agencies, and animal welfare partners.
Represent the organization at events and in media, strengthening its visibility and leadership in the community and sector.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree in Nonprofit Management, Business Administration, Public Administration, or a related field preferred.
Minimum of 5 years of senior leadership experience, preferably within nonprofit organizations, with demonstrated success in organizational leadership, financial management, and strategic planning.
Proven success in fundraising, donor engagement, and cultivating donor relationships.
Experience working with or reporting to a Board of Directors, with knowledge of nonprofit governance.
Experience overseeing multi-department operations and complex organizational structures.
Experience in animal welfare, social services, or mission-driven organizations preferred.
Strong team leadership and organizational development skills.
Strong written, verbal, and public speaking skills, with the ability to build partnerships and represent the organization publicly.
Strong decision-making and problem-solving skills.
Commitment to the mission and values of Animal Humane New Mexico.

Who We Are!

Mountain View Community Development (MVCD) was formalized in 2022 as an outgrowth from Mountain View Fellowship to care for unhoused neighbors. The church began hosting a winter shelter, cooling shelter, and access to shower and laundry in partnership with local service providers. Position Summary:

Our Commitment to Equity

The Y actively promotes a culture free from bias and injustice. We are dedicated to removing institutional and systemic barriers that result in oppression and racism. Job Summary

The Program Director III, Arlington Drive reports directly to the Y Social Impact Center’s Housing and Homeless Services Executive Director and will direct and oversee service delivery, building oversight, and community programming at Arlington Drive Apartments located in Tacoma, WA. Arlington Drive Apartments is a 58-unit housing facility serving young adult individuals and families experiencing or at risk of homelessness. This one-of-a-kind housing facility specifically designed to house unhoused young adults in Pierce County is owned and managed by the Tacoma Housing Authority (THA). THA provides building maintenance and tenant management in partnership with the Y, who provides case management, life skill development, rental assistance, and independent living planning for Arlington residents. The position also oversees several additional community-based contracts and other funding streams that support Arlington Drive and the broader Pierce County Community. The Program Director III, Arlington Drive oversees and supervises a diverse team of multi-level leaders including a supervisor and case managers who work directly with Arlington Drive residents and staff the building 24/7 providing onsite safety and support to residents all day, every day Monday-Sunday.

This position is part of the Y Social Impact Center, the social services branch of the YMCA of Greater Seattle (YGS). The mission of Y Social Impact Center is to accelerate young people’s ability to build safe, successful and happy lives. Every year, we serve 5,000 children, youth, young adults, and families across King County with programs that aim to strengthen young people’s ability to develop to their fullest potential through four strategies: reducing risk factors; navigating systems towards successful life transition; ensuring stability, safety and wellness in times of crisis; and building competencies and social capital. Y Social Impact Center’s programs include housing, behavioral health, foster care licensing, violence prevention, education, and employment. Many of the young people we serve have had involvement in the foster care, criminal justice system, and/or homelessness systems.

East Bay Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (East Bay SPCA), founded in 1874, is proud to be one of the oldest shelters in the country and one of the most innovative in their region. They are a local non-profit that is not affiliated with any national organization. The organization is comprised of a strategic and engaged Board of Directors, experienced executive leadership, and a talented, energetic, dedicated and committed staff.

The organization is supported by approximately 100 staff and 500+ active volunteers. They have an annual operating budget of approximately $14 million and an endowment of $30 million. Their main campus is located in Oakland, with an adoption center in Dublin and spay/neuter surgery center also in Oakland.

In 2025, East Bay SPCA facilitated more than 2,700 adoptions, distributed pet food to nearly 700 households, and benefited from more than 35,000 volunteer hours.

The President & CEO reports directly to the Board of Directors.

It’s a desperate gamble that San Francisco Compute does not force you to play.

Originally, SFC was an AI lab that bought too big of a GPU cluster and was forced to sublease it or go under. Today, we build data centers, supercomputers, and then lease those machines on contracts that let our customers sublease. More than anyone else in the industry, we deeply felt the pain and fear of being forced to bet the farm with your neocloud vendor. To make it possible to sublease, we invented the first compute market and became the first one to offer physical settlement. That means we operate GPU clusters like a neocloud and derisk our customers like a market.

Customers buying GPU clusters don’t want to work through a network of brokers. They want to transact with the folks that have the keys to the cluster and can own the SLA.

To keep the industry safe from unnecessary risk, SFC needs to scale fast. To do that, we serve financially motivated parties as a technical partner to build, operate, & lease supercomputers on their behalf. Basically, we help folks who want an economic return build GPU clusters on their balance sheet, but operated in full by us. That allows us to retain the technical control needed to operate a cloud, but scale fast like a market. SFC’s ability to offer subleasing can significantly increase the levered returns for cluster owners. Our hybrid model out-performs brokered contracts or other “compute markets”, who have to go through a network of counterparties to solve problems. It also lets us design custom solutions for our customers, like clusters deployed in regions next to your dataset or physical eval set or a large CPU fleet deployed colocated with your GPU cluster.

Our team includes senior & technical leadership from places like Lambda, Crusoe, Digital Ocean, AWS, and Hut8. Our CTO is the cofounder and former CEO of Voltage Park. In prior roles, our team has deployed 8GW of datacenter capacity & hundreds of thousands of GPUs. We’ve been described as having “the highest talent density in the space.” If you are an honorable, gritty person with eyes wide open & good epistemics, who wants to see AI go right, we’d love to work with you. There has never been a more critical moment in history and it is up to us to shape it on behalf of those who come after us.
